title: v2.13 adds Gateway API support (ALBGatewayAPI / NLBGatewayAPI feature gates) built against Gateway API v1.2.0 CRDs

detection.reason: checked the Gateway API CRDs' gateway.networking.k8s.io/bundle-version annotation (projected as bundleVersion) — a bundle below v1.2.0 is older than what v2.13 was built against

remediation: Only when turning the Gateway API feature gates on: install the Gateway API v1.2.0 standard CRDs (experimental for TCP/UDP routes) and the LBC gateway CRDs (config/crd/gateway/gateway-crds.yaml) first. The gates are off by default in 2.13, so nothing changes for Ingress-only clusters.

gate.reason: the Gateway API CRD requirement only bites clusters that run Gateway API routes under this controller — with no route of any kind in the snapshot the controller has nothing to serve

verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group == "gateway.networking.k8s.io") | "\(.metadata.name) bundle=\(.metadata.annotations["gateway.networking.k8s.io/bundle-version"] // "-") served=\([.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] | join(","))"'  # the installed Gateway API CRD bundle version and the API versions each route CRD still serves

title: IngressClassParams gains prefixListsIDs and targetType, and the gateway.k8s.aws CRDs arrive — apply the CRDs by hand under Helm

detection.reason: reads the installed CRD's top-level spec field names (crdSpecFields[], agent 0.4.154+); IngressClassParams PrefixListsIDs (with targetType) is v2.13.0's addition; the new gateway.k8s.aws CRDs are not checked — an older agent writes no field list, which reads not projected, never clean

quote: We’ve added new fields to the IngressClassParams CRD. Please apply the latest CRD definitions: kubectl apply -k "github.com/aws/eks-charts/stable/aws-load-balancer-controller/crds?ref=master"
remediation: Run kubectl apply -k "github.com/aws/eks-charts/stable/aws-load-balancer-controller/crds?ref=master" before upgrading when installed with helm.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd ingressclassparams.elbv2.k8s.aws -o json | jq -r '[.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] as $v | (.spec.versions[] | select(.storage) | .schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec.properties // {} | keys) as $k | "served=\($v | join(",")) spec fields=\($k | join(","))"'  # the installed CRD schema; prefixListsIDs/targetType absent from the field list means the CRDs were not re-applied for this release
coversNotes: ingress_class.md › spec.targetType › If the field is specified, LBC will ignore the alb.ingress.

title: Reference IAM policy gains ec2:DescribeRouteTables (subnet discovery by reachability)

detection.reason: IAM lives in AWS; the hint names the controller Deployment whose role to simulate

remediation: Apply the v2.13.0 reference IAM policy before upgrading: the SubnetDiscoveryByReachability gate is ON by default in 2.13, and when no subnet in the VPC carries a kubernetes.io/role/elb or internal-elb tag the controller now reads route tables to tell public from private subnets — AccessDenied there fails the reconcile of every load balancer that relies on untagged-subnet discovery. Clusters with role-tagged subnets never reach the call.
verifyCommand: SA=$(kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.image? // "" | test("aws-load-balancer-controller")) | "\(.metadata.namespace) \(.spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName)"' | head -1); ROLE=$(kubectl get sa -n ${SA% *} ${SA##* } -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.eks\.amazonaws\.com/role-arn}'); aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn "$ROLE" --action-names ec2:DescribeRouteTables --query 'EvaluationResults[].[EvalActionName,EvalDecision]' --output text  # every row must read allowed; implicitDeny means the controller's IAM policy predates this release (Pod Identity: read the association's role with aws eks list-pod-identity-associations --cluster-name ... --namespace ... --service-account ...)
